items.title: Mozambican and Indian companies move Delhi HC alleging ICC arbitrator did not disclose conflict of interest
items.summary: A Mozambican and an Indian company have approached the Delhi High Court challenging a partial award passed by an International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) arbitral tribunal. They have alleged that the presiding arbitrator failed to disclose material appointments and past criminal proceedings against him. The petitions, filed by Black Gold Resources Private Limitada (BGR) and Trident Chemphar Limited (TCL), have challenged the tribunal’s 2:1 decision to include TCL to the arbitration between BGR and Minas De Benga Limitada (MDB) despite being a non-signatory to the contract. The dispute arose from a Mozambican coal mining contract. The Tribunal was presided over by Professor Sundra Rajoo . Former Supreme Court Justice L Nageswara Rao and one DK Singh were co-arbitrators. On May 5 this year, the tribunal delivered a split verdict. While Professor Rajoo and Justice Rao held that TCL, BGR’s Indian shareholder, could be brought into the arbitration, Singh dissented. BGR and TCL then approached the High Court. Justice Sachin Datta heard the challenge today and issued notices to MDB and said that the matter will be heard in October. items.title: Supreme Court seeks structured plan to fix vacancies, pendency in district and state consumer commissions
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed all States to respond within 3 weeks to a status report submitted by Amicus Curiae highlighting vacancies in district and state consumer commissions. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed States to explain compliance with its July 22, 2026 order on pay and allowances for commission members. Pertinently, the Court also took note of a report by the President of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) on vacancies and pendency in consumer commissions. The Court said that the report submitted by the NCDRC President requires serious consideration. Key concerns raised in the report included the appointment process for commission members and the transition to a new enactment, with members under the old regime continuing only until September 6. Attorney General R Venkataramani suggested that selection processes which had begun under the old law may be completed subject to the terms and conditions prescribed under the new enactment. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday directed the Delhi government to expedite the process of filling vacancies in Delhi's Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA). It was stated that the Chairperson's post fell vacant on August 11, 2026, after Kumar turned 65, while a member's post has been vacant since December 2025. items.title: Elephants have rights: Karnataka High Court quashes land acquisition for housing project near Bannerghatta
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed the acquisition of over 1,938 acres of land for the 4th phase of Suryanagar housing project by Karnataka Housing Board (KHB), holding that the project would have irreversible ecological and wildlife-related consequences [Puttarajamma v State of Karnataka] . A division bench of Justices DK Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan passed the judgment while allowing the appeals filed by the landowners against the acquisition of their agricultural land for Suryanagar 4th Phase Layout. The Court observed that while the Suryanagar project seeks to provide affordable and planned housing plots, it would deprive the wildlife of their natural habitat. It added that the project would seriously affect the Karadikkal-Madeshwara Corridor for elephants. “The elephants in question, for whom these corridors constitute not merely a passage but an essential part of their natural habitat and existence, cannot be treated as occupants without rights whose homes may be displaced at will,” the Bench said. items.title: Madras High Court sets aside ban on temples acquiring elephants
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Wednesday set aside a single-judge’s direction prohibiting temples in Tamil Nadu from acquiring elephants [Arulmigu Sri Subramania Swami Thirukoil vs Sheik Mohammed]. A Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan held that the direction travelled beyond the case concerning a female elephant, and affected temples that were neither parties to the proceedings nor were given an opportunity to be heard. The Court, however, affirmed all directions issued for the custody of the elephant, Lalitha, her medical treatment, retirement and welfare. The Division Bench said that a court exercising writ jurisdiction must ordinarily confine the relief to the pleadings and the parties before it. “ This is not a technicality. It is the very foundation of a fair hearing. However well-intentioned a direction may be, it cannot be sustained if it is passed against persons who were strangers to the proceeding and who had no opportunity to place their case before the court ,” the judgment said. items.title: Delhi High Court seeks response from State, MCD on PIL flagging lack of burial spaces for Christians
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Delhi government, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and Delhi Development Authority (DDA) on a plea highlighting lack of cemeteries and burial grounds for Christians. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia observed that under the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, one of the functions assigned to the MCD is to regulate and maintain places meant for disposal of the dead. “It thus appears that it is one of the primary functions assigned to MCD to arrange for spaces where the citizens of the city can observe last rites such as burial grounds and cemeteries," the Court said. Therefore, it directed the MCD to give details of the Christian cemeteries/burial grounds within its territorial jurisdiction and also the space available for the said purpose. The matter will be heard next on November 4.
